plan.estimand: Population R-squared in a linear regression model with 3 predictors
plan.hypothesis: H₀: R² = 0 (all regression coefficients equal zero) versus H₁: R² > 0
assumptions: Linear regression model with intercept and exactly 3 predictors
Null hypothesis: R² = 0 (equivalently, all partial regression slopes equal zero)
Test statistic follows noncentral F distribution under the alternative
Normality and homoscedasticity of errors assumed
Fixed predictor values (design matrix is fixed)
One-sided test (testing whether R² > 0)
Population multiple correlation ρ = 0.30, hence population R² = ρ² = 0.09
scientific_notes: Sample size calculation for overall F test of R² in linear regression uses the noncentral F distribution with numerator df = p (number of predictors) and denominator df = N - p - 1
Noncentrality parameter λ relates to R² via: λ = R² × (N - p - 1) / (1 - R²)
Effect size can be expressed as f² = R² / (1 - R²), where f² ≈ 0.0989 for R² = 0.09
This is a test of whether all predictors collectively explain significant variance, not a test of individual coefficients

answer.summary: For a fixed linear regression model with intercept and 3 predictors testing whether population R-squared differs from zero, with anticipated multiple correlation ρ = 0.30 (hence R² = 0.09), α = 0.05, and target power = 90%, the minimum integer total sample size is 149 participants. This design achieves an actual power of 90.13%. The preceding candidate design (N = 148) yields 89.92% power, confirming that 149 is the smallest admissible size meeting the criterion.
answer.method: Noncentral F test for overall regression. The test statistic under the null hypothesis (R² = 0) follows a central F distribution with df₁ = p = 3 and df₂ = N − p − 1. Under the alternative hypothesis with population R² = 0.09, the test statistic follows a noncentral F distribution with the same degrees of freedom and noncentrality parameter λ = f² × df₂, where f² = R²/(1 − R²) ≈ 0.0989. Power is computed as P(F(df₁, df₂, λ) > F_{crit}(α, df₁, ∞)), where F_{crit} ≈ 2.605 for α = 0.05 and df₁ = 3. A binary search identified the minimum N for which power ≥ 0.90.
assumptions: Fixed linear regression model with intercept and exactly 3 predictors
Null hypothesis: population R² = 0 (all regression slopes equal zero); alternative: R² > 0
Errors are independent and normally distributed with constant variance (homoscedasticity)
Predictor values are fixed (or treated as fixed conditional on their observed values)
Population multiple correlation ρ = 0.30, hence population R² = 0.09
Test is one-sided at α = 0.05 (testing whether any variance is explained)
Inversion uses the noncentral F distribution with no finite-sample correction factors
limitations: No attrition or dropout adjustment; sample size is for enrolled participants with complete data
Calculation assumes the model is correctly specified and that predictors' joint distribution matches the design assumptions
Monte Carlo simulation was not performed; results rely on the noncentral F approximation, which is exact for normal errors under fixed design assumptions
If predictors are random (not fixed), adjustments to the model and power calculation may be needed
The design assumes homogeneity of variance across predictor space; violation of this assumption may reduce actual power

executions.code:
# Parameters
p <- 3                    # number of predictors
rho <- 0.30               # anticipated multiple correlation coefficient
R_squared <- rho^2        # R-squared = 0.09
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level
target_power <- 0.90      # desired power
f_squared <- R_squared / (1 - R_squared)  # effect size f²

cat("=== Sample Size Calculation for Linear Regression Overall F Test ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of predictors (p): %d\n", p))
cat(sprintf("Population multiple correlation (ρ): %.2f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("Population R²: %.4f\n", R_squared))
cat(sprintf("Effect size (f²): %.6f\n", f_squared))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (α): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Target power: %.2f\n\n", target_power))

# Critical F value for the numerator df = p at alpha = 0.05
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, p, Inf)
cat(sprintf("Critical F value (df1=%d, df2=Inf): %.6f\n\n", p, f_crit))

# Function to compute power at a given sample size N
compute_power <- function(N, p, f_sq, alpha) {
  df1 <- p
  df2 <- N - p - 1
  
  # Noncentrality parameter: λ = f² × df2
  lambda <- f_sq * df2
  
  # Critical F value
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, Inf)
  
  # Power = P(F(df1, df2, λ) > f_crit)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum N that gives power ≥ 0.90
# Start with a reasonable lower bound
N_min <- 5
N_max <- 500
achieved_power <- compute_power(N_max, p, f_squared, alpha)

if (achieved_power < target_power) {
  stop("Sample size of 500 does not achieve target power. Need larger search space.")
}

# Binary search for minimum N
while (N_max - N_min > 1) {
  N_mid <- (N_min + N_max) %/% 2
  power_mid <- compute_power(N_mid, p, f_squared, alpha)
  
  if (power_mid < target_power) {
    N_min <- N_mid
  } else {
    N_max <- N_mid
  }
}

N_opt <- N_max
power_opt <- compute_power(N_opt, p, f_squared, alpha)
N_prev <- N_opt - 1
power_prev <- compute_power(N_prev, p, f_squared, alpha)

cat("=== Results ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Minimum sample size N = %d participants\n", N_opt))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at N = %d: %.6f\n", N_opt, power_opt))
cat(sprintf("Power at preceding design (N = %d): %.6f\n\n", N_prev, power_prev))

# Verify the design
df1 <- p
df2_opt <- N_opt - p - 1
lambda_opt <- f_squared * df2_opt
f_crit_opt <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, Inf)

cat("=== Verification ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Numerator df (p): %d\n", df1))
cat(sprintf("Denominator df (N - p - 1): %d\n", df2_opt))
cat(sprintf("Noncentrality parameter (λ): %.6f\n", lambda_opt))
cat(sprintf("Critical F value: %.6f\n", f_crit_opt))
cat(sprintf("Test statistic under H₁ ~ F(%d, %d, %.6f)\n", df1, df2_opt, lambda_opt))

# Explicit power computation for final verification
power_explicit <- 1 - pf(f_crit_opt, df1, df2_opt, ncp = lambda_opt)
cat(sprintf("Explicit power calculation: %.6f\n\n", power_explicit))

# Output as JSON for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = N_opt, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = power_opt, unit = "unitless"),
    list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = power_prev, unit = "unitless")
  )
)

cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(results, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")
